name: Dotmarket.eu
description: French marketplace for buying / selling digital businesses (SaaS, media, e-commerce, web agencies). Claims 300+ vetted and valued deals a year (company-stated). Registered in Estonia, founded Jan 2020.

mentions.evidence: ~$12,903 MRR, 403 active subscriptions, ~$9,043 L30, ~$1,141,337 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~04:05 Warsaw (02:05 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Run a language-local "buy a small online business" marketplace (PL / CZ / DE) with paid buyer access and valuation packs. Local trust and language are the moat versus Acquire.com.

whyItPrints: Deal-flow subscription. Buyers pay recurring access for vetted listings, sellers pay for valuation/listing. 403 subs at ~$32 average (my calculation) is a classic "small ticket × hundreds of logos" print, and French-language focus keeps Flippa/Acquire away.
whyThisMatters:
Buyers in France shop here for an online business that's already been checked: an e-commerce brand, a SaaS product, a media site, or a web agency. A seller can ask for a valuation first. Each deal is written up and given a price.

They turn most submissions away. The site says 9 percent of projects people send in get published. Buyers then see deals that match what they asked for. Dotmarket School is a four-month course on how to read a digital acquisition. There's weekly coaching, meetups in Paris and other French cities, and a newsletter about exits.

The company is registered in Estonia and started in January 2020. They say they handle more than 300 vetted deals a year. The site is in French. Flippa and Acquire are the English-language marketplaces a buyer might already know.
